provenance.note: Disconfirming case, RE-SCORED on drain rather than trusted. The staged 2026-06-23 quote ('The Annals of Mathematics does not consider papers generated using AI products') is GONE from the live page — the policy has LOOSENED from a flat refusal to consider AI-generated papers into a disclose-and-locate rule. Re-scored 7/12 -> 10/12, posture Prohibitive -> Balanced. c2_fit stays 'deviates': mathematics has the cheapest verification economics of any field (proof is mechanically checkable), yet the Annals now draws exactly the same permit-vs-reserve line as biomedical and social-science publishers whose proof is expensive, and still never cites verifiability as the reason. Cheap proof did not buy more machine latitude — it bought the same line. Drained from tranche-1-staged-2026-06-23.
